newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian lamb prices to remain high - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australian lamb prices to remain high - ABARE.

text.p: Australian lamb saleyard prices are expected to remain relatively high in 1997/98 (July-June) at 207 cents a kilogram, the Australian Bureau of Agricultral and Resources Economic (ABARE) said.
However, higher procuction levels would see prices around 2.0 percent below that of ABARE's 1996/97 estimate of 211 cents.

"Although below average seasonal conditions may affect Australian production of lamb in 1997/98, output is forecast to increase 3.0 percent as producers respond to continued high lamb prices," ABARE said in its June quarter review.
Dry seasonal conditions affecting key sheep producing areas in Australia's eastern states in the first quarter of 1997 have resulted in a moderate increase in adult sheep slaughterings.
However, seasonal conditions permitting, continued high lamb prices and rising wool prices were likely to influence producers to retain sheep for flock building in 1997/98, ABARE said.
"As a result, a reduction in sheep slaughterings is forecast to lead to an almost 3.0 percent fall in mutton production to 283,000 tonnes," ABARE said.
Mutton prices were forecast to increase marginally, to 68 cents in 1997/98, it added.
